messages:
alex: following yesterday's postmortem, quick sync on outstanding remediation items and who takes ownership. TL;DR we need clear owners, jira links, and a short timeline.
maria: agree. I've pulled the list from the doc — several items are low-effort but unassigned. suggest triage this afternoon.
sam: I can own the cache-eviction followup (PMT-7192). will do a quick investigation and post findings by EOD Thu. assigning R: sam, A: maria, C: raj, I: alex.
raj: noted. i'll be consulted for the rollout plan. can we add a rollback checklist to the ticket? saw similar regressions last quarter.
jess: adding to ticket: PMT-7192 -> notes about rollback + test plan. also adding label `remediation:priority-medium`.
alex: perfect. for the KV-cache TTL mismatch (PMT-7210) we need someone to own the temporal analysis. @raj can you take that? it's linked in the postmortem under 'recurring pattern: TTL drift'. :eyes:
raj: I can. ETA next Tue morning. i'll also synthesize the recurring incidents and attach a short graph.
maria: quick ask — can we standardize owners as `R` and a single `A` per item to avoid two people owning acceptance? last time that caused confusion.
sam: +1. i'll take R on 7192 and ask @maria to be A for validation.
oncall-bot: Incident PMT-7192 assigned to sam; reminder set for 2026-04-02T15:00:00Z.
jess: heads up — PMT-7255 (autoscaler spike) looks like a config drift. small fix but impacts Dedicated customers. propose R: maria, A: alex, C: eng-sre, I: sales.
alex: agreed on PMT-7255. maria, can you add an owner-runbook step and add a canary plan? if it's high-risk we should schedule a canary window.
maria: scheduled canary window Mon 09:00 UTC. adding playbook snippet to the ticket: ```
# Canary steps
1. deploy config to canary pool
2. monitor token latency > 2m windows
3. revert if error rate > 0.5% or latency spike > 30%
```
sam: question — for recurring pattern analysis, do we want a recurring postmortem section in the runbook or a separate 'repeat incidents' board?
raj: separate board preferred. makes it easier to track mitigation progress over time vs. one-off PM items. i'll create a lightweight dashboard in Grafana and link to tickets.
jess: created PMT-7300 as the 'recurring-incident-tracker' epic. linking 7192, 7210, 7255. please add your tickets as children.
alex: good. let's lock timelines: 7192 (sam) EOD Thu, 7210 (raj) Tue next week, 7255 (maria) canary Mon. we'll do a 15m sync on Mon 10:30 UTC to confirm rollout. @everyone please update Jira with exact acceptance criteria.
maria: filing acceptance criteria now (unit tests + smoke test runbook + rollback steps).
sam: will post my investigation log to PMT-7192 and ping once the fix is in canary.
raj: adding the recurring-incidents dashboard draft link: https://grafana.internal/r/recurring-incidents (WIP). feedback welcome.
alex: thanks all. one last thing — who will own the RACI doc update to reflect these new lanes? we should avoid repeated handoffs.
jess: I can update the RACI doc and add a section for "postmortem handback" with owner rotation notes. will create a PR and ping.
oncall-bot: Reminder: postmortem follow-up sync scheduled in 48h.
alex: awesome. closing the loop — i'll mark the postmortem thread as 'followup in progress' and we reconvene Mon 10:30. :thumbsup:
